Exploring turbidity fluctuations

Source: vignettes/turbidity.Rmd
turbidity.Rmd

This is an example workflow of how to perform basic turbidity analysis with loadflux package and tidyverse ecosystem.

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(loadflux)

Hydrological Events

First, we need to demarcate hydrological events

data(djanturb)
df <- hydro_events(dataframe = djanturb,
                   q = discharge,
                   datetime = time,
                   window = 21)

df |> 
  event_plot(q = discharge,
             datetime = time,
             he = he,
             ssc = ntu,
             y2label = "Turbidity")

Turbidity Index

Then we can calculate Turbidity Index TI for every hydrological event


TI_index <- df |> 
  group_by(he) |> 
  nest() |> 
  mutate(
    TI = vapply(data, function(x) TI(x, ntu, time), numeric(1))
  ) |> 
  select(-data) |> 
  ungroup()

TI_index
#> # A tibble: 6 × 2
#>      he    TI
#>   <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     1 0.193
#> 2     2 0.113
#> 3     3 0.147
#> 4     4 0.153
#> 5     5 0.108
#> 6     6 0.137

Hydrological event parameters

Start, end, and duration of each event used to go through tsibble and feat_event. The same numbers are a grouped summary of time:

event_params <- df |>
  group_by(he) |>
  summarise(
    start = min(time),
    end = max(time),
    length = difftime(end, start, units = "h"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

event_params
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>      he start               end                 length        
#>   <dbl> <dttm>              <dttm>              <drtn>        
#> 1     1 2016-06-16 09:30:00 2016-06-17 10:50:00 25.33333 hours
#> 2     2 2016-06-17 11:00:00 2016-06-18 09:50:00 22.83333 hours
#> 3     3 2016-06-18 10:00:00 2016-06-19 12:20:00 26.33333 hours
#> 4     4 2016-06-19 12:30:00 2016-06-20 11:00:00 22.50000 hours
#> 5     5 2016-06-20 12:00:00 2016-06-21 11:20:00 23.33333 hours
#> 6     6 2016-06-21 11:40:00 2016-06-22 10:20:00 22.66667 hours

A five-number summary of turbidity per event used to come from brolgar::feat_five_num. That is also a grouped summary:

ntu_summary <- df |>
  group_by(he) |>
  summarise(
    min = min(ntu, na.rm = TRUE),
    q25 = stats::quantile(ntu, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE),
    median = stats::median(ntu, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75 = stats::quantile(ntu, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE),
    max = max(ntu, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ntu_summary
#> # A tibble: 6 × 6
#>      he   min   q25 median   q75   max
#>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     1 133.  194.    348.  490. 1018.
#> 2     2 126.  225.    306.  439. 1209.
#> 3     3  83.4 118.    154.  224.  520.
#> 4     4  62.4  87.0   114.  195   451.
#> 5     5  51.8  63.4    76   105.  374.
#> 6     6  81.3 121.    164   262. 1364.
